context: Judges 20:45-48 and 21:1-3: survivors flee to Rimmon; Israel destroys the Benjaminite settlements; the following chapter laments the missing tribe.

source_interpretation.working_preference: Published alternative מְתִם, defective plural men, in the expression city of men / inhabited city
source_interpretation.selection_status: provisional; codex pointing and historical priority unresolved
source_interpretation.strongest_objection: Entire-city interpretation remains possible; UXLC reports both points; Greek forms do not uniquely support the selected pointing.

intended_improvement: Clarify the human-to-livestock range and disclose its source interpretation; do not claim a new massacre narrative or a doctrine change.
policy: Keep sons of Benjamin, edge of the sword, the exhaustive destruction, and the final city-burning clause. City may be collective, but plural inhabitants must be acknowledged as interpretation. Do not add a claim that every inhabitant died or identify the humans exclusively as soldiers.
close_gloss: And the man/men of Israel returned against the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the mouth/edge of the sword, from city of men to livestock, to all that was found; also all the cities that were found they sent into fire.
order_basis: Manually permuted, not randomized; identities withheld from a fresh-context reviewer, not a corpus-wide blind benchmark.

candidates.R: And the men of Israel turned back against the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword—the inhabitants of the cities, the livestock, even all that was found. Also all the cities that were found they set on fire.
candidates.S: And the men of Israel turned back against the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword, from each city, men to livestock, even all that was found. Also all the cities that were found they set on fire.
